facts.statement: Libycosuchus is an extinct genus of North African crocodyliform that is possibly related to Notosuchus.
facts.quote: Libycosuchus is an extinct genus of North African crocodyliform possibly related to Notosuchus

facts.statement: The genus belongs to the monotypic family Libycosuchidae and subfamily Libycosuchinae.
facts.quote: It is part of the monotypic Libycosuchidae and Libycosuchinae

facts.statement: The animal lived approximately 95 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: living approximately 95 million years ago in the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Libycosuchus have been found in the Bahariya Formation in Egypt.
facts.quote: Fossil remains have been found in the Bahariya Formation in Egypt

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in the early 1910s by Richard Markgraf.
facts.quote: The holotype was discovered during the early 1910s by Richard Markgraf

facts.statement: The type species L. brevirostris was named in 1914 and formally described in 1915.
facts.quote: the type species, L. brevirostis, was named in 1914 and described in 1915

facts.statement: Libycosuchus is classified within the parent group Eunotosuchia.
The time range for Libycosuchus is estimated between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Libycosuchus was one of the few fossils described by Ernst Stromer that survived the bombing of Munich in 1944.
rejected.quote: It was one of the few fossils described by Ernst Stromer that wasn't destroyed by the Royal Air Force during the bombing of Munich in 1944
